      theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.coordinateZariski_isOpen_injective_matrix {k : Type u_1} {σ : Type u_2} {X : Type u_3} [Field k] (c : X → σ → k) {m : Type u_4} {n : Type u_5} [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (A : Matrix m n (MvPolynomial σ k)) :
      IsOpen {x : X | Function.Injective (A.map ⇑(MvPolynomial.eval (c x))).mulVec}

      Injectivity of a rectangular polynomial matrix is open, including for zero-dimensional source or target. A left inverse at a point gives a square determinant whose nonvanishing certifies injectivity near that point.

      theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.coordinateZariski_isOpen_zero_intertwiners {k : Type u_1} {σ : Type u_2} {X : Type u_3} [Field k] (c : X → σ → k) {a : Type u_4} {m : Type u_5} {n : Type u_6} [Fintype a] [Fintype m] [Fintype n] (L : a → Matrix m m (MvPolynomial σ k)) (R : a → Matrix n n (MvPolynomial σ k)) :
      IsOpen {x : X | ∀ (T : Matrix m n k), (∀ (j : a), (L j).map ⇑(MvPolynomial.eval (c x)) * T = T * (R j).map ⇑(MvPolynomial.eval (c x))) → T = 0}

      For two tuples of action matrices depending polynomially on the same parameters, the locus on which every intertwiner is zero is open.

      theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.coordinateZariski_finite_open_fibers {k : Type u_1} {σ : Type u_2} {X : Type u_3} [Field k] [Finite σ] (c : X → σ → k) {I : Type u_4} (f : X → I) (s : Set I) (represented : s ⊆ Set.range f) (ho : ∀ i ∈ s, IsOpen (f ⁻¹' {i})) :
      s.Finite

      In a finite-coordinate parameter space, only finitely many values of a classifying map can have nonempty open fibers. This applies to the map sending a representation to its isomorphism class.
